QuestionStmt.S: The line of intersection of the planes $\vec{r} \cdot (3\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = 1$ and $\vec{r} \cdot (\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}) = 2$ is parallel to the vector

Solution.S:
The line of intersection is perpendicular to both normal vectors of the planes. Therefore, its direction vector is given by the cross product of the normals.

$$\vec{n_1} = 3\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}, \quad \vec{n_2} = \hat{i} + 4\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$$

$$\vec{n_1} \times \vec{n_2} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 & -2 \end{vmatrix} = -2\hat{i} + 7\hat{j} + 13\hat{k}$$

Thus the line is parallel to $-2\hat{i} + 7\hat{j} + 13\hat{k}$.

Final Answer: $$\boxed{-2\hat{i} + 7\hat{j} + 13\hat{k}}$$

Hence, the correct option is D.
